meaningEn: Basic structure and assembly rules of Korean Hangul syllable blocks.
meaningId: Struktur dasar dan aturan penyusunan blok suku kata Hangul Korea.

notesEn.formation: Syllables are formed in grid blocks: [Consonant + Vowel] or [Consonant + Vowel + Consonant (Batchim)]. Vertical vowels (ㅣ, ㅏ, ㅓ) attach to the right of the consonant. Horizontal vowels (ㅡ, ㅜ, ㅗ) attach below the consonant.
notesEn.usage: Used to compose any readable unit/word in Korean.
notesEn.nuance: Romanization is only an approximation (e.g., ㄱ sounds between G and K, ㄹ between R and L). Learners should rely on audio listening rather than Latin representations.

notesId.formation: Suku kata disusun dalam blok kotak: [Konsonan + Vokal] atau [Konsonan + Vokal + Konsonan (Batchim)]. Vokal vertikal (ㅣ, ㅏ, ㅓ) ditulis di sebelah kanan konsonan. Vokal horizontal (ㅡ, ㅜ, ㅗ) ditulis di bawah konsonan.
notesId.usage: Digunakan untuk menyusun setiap unit/kata yang dapat dibaca dalam bahasa Korea.
notesId.nuance: Romanisasi hanyalah pendekatan (contoh: ㄱ berada di antara G dan K, ㄹ di antara R dan L). Pembelajar sebaiknya mengandalkan pendengaran audio daripada transliterasi Latin.

quiz.question: Which syllable structure is used when pairing a consonant with a horizontal vowel like 'ㅜ' and a final consonant?
options: Consonant on left, Vowel on right, Final Consonant on bottom
Consonant on top, Vowel below it, Final Consonant at the very bottom
Vowel on top, Consonant below it
Final Consonant on top, Vowel on left
quiz.explanationEn: Horizontal vowels (ㅡ, ㅜ, ㅗ) are drawn below the initial consonant, and the final consonant (batchim) is placed underneath them.
quiz.explanationId: Vokal horizontal (ㅡ, ㅜ, ㅗ) ditulis di bawah konsonan awal, dan konsonan akhir (batchim) diletakkan di bagian paling bawah.

fillInTheBlank.hintId: Vokal vertikal ㅏ berada di kanan ㄱ, dan ㄴ berada di bawah.

constructionQuiz.hintId: Gabungkan ㅂ awal, vokal vertikal ㅓ, dan ㅂ akhir.

notesEn.formation: When placed at the initial position (top or left), 'ㅇ' acts as a silent placeholder so the syllable starts with a vowel sound. When placed at the bottom position (batchim), it is pronounced as 'ng'.
notesEn.usage: Essential for fulfilling the rule that every Korean syllable block must start with a consonant.
notesEn.nuance: The same letter 'ㅇ' has two distinct acoustic functions depending purely on its position in the syllable grid.

notesId.formation: Jika diletakkan di posisi awal (atas atau kiri), 'ㅇ' berfungsi sebagai penanda diam (tidak berbunyi) sehingga suku kata diawali bunyi vokal. Jika diletakkan di posisi bawah (batchim), ia dilafalkan sebagai 'ng'.
notesId.usage: Sangat penting untuk memenuhi aturan bahwa setiap blok suku kata Korea harus dimulai dengan konsonan.
notesId.nuance: Huruf 'ㅇ' yang sama memiliki dua fungsi akustik berbeda yang sepenuhnya tergantung pada posisinya di dalam blok suku kata.

examples.meaningId: ㅇ awal tanpa bunyi + ㅏ + ㄴ

quiz.explanationEn: At position 1 (initial position), 'ㅇ' makes no sound and simply allows the syllable to begin with the vowel.
quiz.explanationId: Di posisi 1 (posisi awal), 'ㅇ' tidak bersuara dan hanya memungkinkan suku kata dimulai dengan bunyi vokal.

pattern: Tense & Aspirated Consonants (ㄲ, ㅋ, ㅃ, ㅍ, ㅉ, ㅊ, ㄸ, ㅌ, ㅆ)
meaningEn: Tense (double) and aspirated consonant variations in Hangul.
meaningId: Konsonan tegang (ganda) dan teraspirasi dalam Hangul.

notesEn.formation: Tense consonants (ㄲ, ㅃ, ㅉ, ㄸ, ㅆ) double the basic consonant and are produced with strong vocal cord tension. Aspirated consonants (ㅋ, ㅍ, ㅊ, ㅌ) add an extra stroke and release a strong burst of air.
notesEn.usage: Used to differentiate distinct phonetic sounds in Korean words.
notesEn.nuance: English speakers often struggle to differentiate basic (ㄱ, ㄷ, ㅂ), tense (ㄲ, ㄸ, ㅃ), and aspirated (ㅋ, ㅌ, ㅍ) sounds. Listening to native speakers is crucial.

notesId.formation: Konsonan tegang (ㄲ, ㅃ, ㅉ, ㄸ, ㅆ) menggandakan konsonan dasar dan diucapkan dengan ketegangan pita suara. Konsonan teraspirasi (ㅋ, ㅍ, ㅊ, ㅌ) menambahkan satu garis ekstra dan melepaskan hembusan udara yang kuat.
notesId.usage: Digunakan untuk membedakan bunyi fonetis yang unik dalam kata-kata bahasa Korea.
notesId.nuance: Penutur bahasa Inggris/Indonesia sering kali kesulitan membedakan bunyi dasar (ㄱ, ㄷ, ㅂ), tegang (ㄲ, ㄸ, ㅃ), dan teraspirasi (ㅋ, ㅌ, ㅍ). Mendengarkan penutur asli sangatlah penting.

quiz.explanationId: ㅍ adalah bentuk teraspirasi dari ㅂ, diucapkan dengan hembusan udara (bunyi P).

pattern: Complex Vowels & Diphthongs (ㅑ, ㅕ, ㅠ, ㅛ, ㅐ, ㅔ, ㅟ, ㅝ, ㅚ, ㅘ, ㅢ, ㅖ, etc.)
meaningEn: Complex Korean vowels, Y-vowels, and combined diphthongs.
meaningId: Vokal kompleks, vokal-Y, dan diftong gabungan dalam Hangul.

notesEn.formation: Y-vowels (ㅑ, ㅕ, ㅠ, ㅛ) add an extra line to basic vowels. Combined diphthongs blend two vowels (e.g., ㅜ + ㅣ = ㅟ [wi], ㅗ + ㅏ = ㅘ [wa]). ㅐ and ㅔ sound identical in modern Korean.
notesEn.usage: Used to represent expanded vowel sounds in Korean vocabulary.
notesEn.nuance: Modern Korean speakers pronounce ㅐ and ㅔ identically (like 'e' in 'bed'). Also, ㅚ, ㅙ, and ㅞ all sound virtually identical to 'way'.

notesId.formation: Vokal-Y (ㅑ, ㅕ, ㅠ, ㅛ) menambahkan garis ekstra pada vokal dasar. Diftong gabungan mencampurkan dua vokal (misal: ㅜ + ㅣ = ㅟ [wi], ㅗ + ㅏ = ㅘ [wa]). ㅐ dan ㅔ berbunyi identik dalam bahasa Korea modern.
notesId.usage: Digunakan untuk merepresentasikan bunyi vokal yang diperluas dalam kosakata Korea.
notesId.nuance: Penutur bahasa Korea modern melafalkan ㅐ dan ㅔ secara identik (seperti 'e' pada 'bed'). Selain itu, ㅚ, ㅙ, dan ㅞ semuanya berbunyi hampir persis sama seperti 'way'.

quiz.question: How are ㅐ and ㅔ pronounced in modern Korean?

ㅐ is silent while ㅔ is stressed
ㅐ is pronounced only at the end of sentences
quiz.explanationEn: Historically distinct, ㅐ and ㅔ have merged in modern spoken Korean and sound completely identical.
quiz.explanationId: Secara historis berbeda, ㅐ dan ㅔ telah menyatu dalam pengucapan bahasa Korea modern dan terdengar sama persis.

notesEn.formation: Noun + 이 (if noun ends in consonant) / 가 (if noun ends in vowel) + 있다.
notesEn.usage: Expresses possession ('to have'). Because 있다 is grammatically an adjective in Korean, the possessed item takes the subject marker ~이/가 rather than the object marker ~을/를.
notesEn.nuance: Never use ~을/를 with 있다 to mean 'have'. Using ~을/를 있다 is grammatically incorrect in Korean.

notesId.formation: Kata Benda + 이 (jika berakhiran konsonan) / 가 (jika berakhiran vokal) + 있다.
notesId.usage: Expresses possession ('mempunyai/memiliki'). Karena 있다 secara tata bahasa adalah kata sifat dalam bahasa Korea, objek yang dimiliki menggunakan penanda subjek ~이/가 bukan penanda objek ~을/를.
notesId.nuance: Jangan pernah menggunakan ~을/를 dengan 있다 untuk arti 'memiliki'. Menggunakan ~을/를 있다 adalah salah secara tata bahasa.

quiz.question: Which particle must be attached to '가방' in the sentence 'I have a bag'?
quiz.explanationEn: Because 있다 is an adjective, the object possessed takes ~이/가 (가방 ends in a consonant, so ~이).
quiz.explanationId: Karena 있다 adalah kata sifat, objek yang dimiliki menggunakan ~이/가 (가방 berakhiran konsonan, jadi ~이).

constructionQuiz.promptId: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Korea: 'Aku punya pulpen.'
constructionQuiz.hintEn: Use subject topic 나는, 펜 + particle 이, and 있다.
constructionQuiz.hintId: Gunakan topik 나는, 펜 + partikel 이, dan 있다.

notesEn.usage: Indicates that a person or thing exists at/in a specific place.
notesEn.nuance: Differs from 'N이/가 있다' (to have). Changing particle from ~가/이 to ~에 changes meaning from 'have N' to 'be at N'. For example, '학교가 있다' = 'have a school', while '학교에 있다' = 'be at school'.

notesId.usage: Menunjukkan bahwa seseorang atau sesuatu berada/ada di lokasi tertentu.
notesId.nuance: Berbeda dari 'N이/가 있다' (memiliki). Mengubah partikel dari ~가/이 ke ~에 mengubah arti dari 'memiliki N' menjadi 'berada di N'. Contoh: '학교가 있다' = 'punya sekolah', sedangkan '학교에 있다' = 'ada di sekolah'.

quiz.question: What is the difference between '나는 학교가 있다' and '나는 학교에 있다'?
options: The first means 'I have a school', the second means 'I am at school'
The first means 'I am at school', the second means 'I have a school'
quiz.explanationEn: ~가 indicates possession with 있다 ('have school'), whereas ~에 indicates existence in a location ('be at school').
quiz.explanationId: ~가 menunjukkan kepemilikan dengan 있다 ('punya sekolah'), sedangkan ~에 menunjukkan keberadaan di lokasi ('ada di sekolah').

pattern: N + 이/가 vs. N + 은/는 (Subject vs. Topic Nuance)

notesEn.formation: Consonant + 이 / 은; Vowel + 가 / 는.
notesEn.usage: ~이/가 marks the grammatical subject stating a raw fact. ~은/는 sets the topic or implies comparison/contrast with something else.
notesEn.nuance: For instance, '고양이가 집 뒤에 있다' states the fact that the cat is behind the house. '고양이는 집 뒤에 있다' implies comparison (e.g. 'The dog is inside, but the cat is behind the house').

notesId.formation: Konsonan + 이 / 은; Vokal + 가 / 는.
notesId.usage: ~이/가 menandai subjek tata bahasa yang menyatakan fakta mentah. ~은/는 menetapkan topik atau mengindikasikan perbandingan/kontras dengan hal lain.
notesId.nuance: Sebagai contoh, '고양이가 집 뒤에 있다' menyatakan fakta bahwa kucing ada di belakang rumah. '고양이는 집 뒤에 있다' menyiratkan perbandingan (misal: 'Anjing ada di dalam, tetapi kalau kucing ada di belakang rumah').
